en: make sprout; put out (shoots); clear (a path)

examples.en: When spring comes, the seeds sprout.
I tried sprouting beans on the balcony.

examples.ko: 저는 화분에 해바라기 싹을 틔우고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to get a sunflower to sprout in a pot.
I'm waiting until the tree puts out new shoots.

examples.ko: 이 씨앗은 물에 불리면 싹을 더 빨리 틔워요.
examples.en: If you soak these seeds, they sprout faster.
Thank you for clearing the blocked waterway.

explain: '싹이 트다'는 싹이 스스로 나올 때, '싹을 틔우다'는 씨앗이나 사람이 싹을 내는 쪽에서 말해요. 발음은 [티우다]예요. 막힌 길이나 물길을 열어 줄 때도 쓰지만 일상 대화에서는 주로 싹과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: '싹이 트다' is used when a sprout comes out by itself, while '싹을 틔우다' looks at it from the seed or the person making it sprout. It is pronounced [티우다]. It can also mean opening a blocked path or waterway, but in daily talk it mostly appears with sprouts.

en: broken mirror; end of marriage; divorce

examples.ko: 두 사람의 결혼은 결국 파경을 맞았어요.
examples.en: Their marriage eventually fell apart.

examples.ko: 오랜 갈등 끝에 부부 관계가 파경에 이르렀어요.
examples.en: After a long conflict, the couple's relationship reached a breakup.

examples.ko: 연예인 부부의 파경 소식이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: News of the celebrity couple's split came out.

examples.ko: 파경을 막으려고 두 사람이 상담을 받았어요.
examples.en: The two of them went to counseling to prevent a breakup.
My friends' marriage is on the verge of breaking up, so I'm worried.
What do you think caused the breakup?

explain: 주로 부부 사이가 끝나는 일에 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '이혼'이나 '헤어지다'라고 말하고, '파경'은 뉴스와 글에서 많이 나와요. '파경을 맞다', '파경에 이르다'처럼 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for the end of a marriage. In daily talk people say '이혼' or '헤어지다', while '파경' appears often in news and writing. It is commonly used in set patterns like '파경을 맞다' and '파경에 이르다'.

examples.en: The plan failed and led to a catastrophic result.

examples.ko: 파국적 상황이 오기 전에 문제를 해결해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to solve the problem before a catastrophic situation arrives.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 갈등은 파국적 단계에 들어섰어요.
examples.en: The conflict between the two countries has entered a catastrophic stage.

examples.ko: 환경 문제를 방치하면 파국적 영향이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we ignore environmental problems, catastrophic effects can occur.

examples.ko: 그 사고는 회사에 파국적 타격을 줬어요.
examples.en: That accident dealt a catastrophic blow to the company.
Everyone tried hard to avoid a catastrophic ending.

explain: 뒤에 명사가 바로 와서 '파국적 결과'처럼 쓰고, '파국적인 결과'라고도 많이 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '최악의', '끔찍한'이라고 하는 경우가 많고, '파국적'은 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A noun follows it directly, as in '파국적 결과', and '파국적인 결과' is also very common. In daily talk people often say '최악의' or '끔찍한' instead, while '파국적' appears more in news and writing.

examples.en: The fish is flapping around inside the net.
The bird took off, flapping its wings.
The baby bird is flapping in its nest.
The fish I caught kept flapping on the ground.

examples.ko: 나비가 꽃 위에서 날개를 파닥거리는 게 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a butterfly flapping its wings over a flower.
The child is playing in the water, flapping his arms and legs.

explain: 작고 가벼운 것이 빠르고 짧게 움직이는 모습에 써요. 더 큰 새나 힘이 센 움직임에는 '퍼덕거리다'를 쓰기도 해요. 새, 물고기, 나비 날개에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes small, light things moving quickly in short motions. For bigger birds or stronger movements, people sometimes use '퍼덕거리다' instead. It fits birds, fish and butterfly wings well.

examples.en: I'm cold and my body is trembling.

examples.ko: 아이가 겁에 질려 파들파들 떨고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is trembling with fear.

examples.ko: 손이 파들파들 떨려서 글씨를 못 쓰겠어요.
examples.en: My hand is shaking so much that I can't write.
The puppy shivers in the winter wind.
I was nervous and my legs were trembling.
My voice trembles when I give a presentation.

explain: 거의 항상 '떨다', '떨리다'와 같이 나와요. 일상에서는 '덜덜'도 많이 쓰고, 화가 나거나 힘을 줘서 떨 때는 '부들부들'이라고 해요. '파들파들'은 작고 가볍게 떠는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It almost always appears with '떨다' or '떨리다'. In daily talk '덜덜' is also very common, and '부들부들' is used when shaking from anger or straining. '파들파들' gives a feel of small, light trembling.

examples.en: He lied and didn't even apologize. That's really shameless.

examples.ko: 파렴치한 행동을 하는 사람은 신뢰할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't trust someone who behaves shamelessly.

examples.ko: 친구 돈을 가져가 놓고 모른 척하다니 파렴치하네요.
examples.en: Taking a friend's money and pretending not to know is shameless.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 너무 파렴치해서 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: He is so shameless that you can't reason with him.

examples.ko: 파렴치하게 남의 아이디어를 가져다 쓰면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not shamelessly take other people's ideas.

examples.ko: 자기 잘못을 남 탓으로 돌리는 건 파렴치한 일이에요.
examples.en: Blaming others for your own mistake is a shameless thing to do.

explain: '뻔뻔하다'는 일상에서 가볍게도 쓰지만, '파렴치하다'는 부끄러움을 모르고 도덕적으로 나쁜 일을 한다는 비난이 더 강해요. 사람이나 행동을 나무랄 때 쓰고, 반대로 부끄러움을 아는 사람은 '염치 있다'고 해요.
explain_en: '뻔뻔하다' can be used lightly in daily talk, but '파렴치하다' carries a stronger moral criticism of someone who does wrong without any shame. It is used to condemn a person or an act. A person who does feel shame is described as '염치 있다'.

examples.ko: 봄이 오자 들판에 새싹이 파릇파릇 돋아요.
examples.en: When spring comes, new sprouts come up green in the fields.
Green onions are growing fresh and green in the pot.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤에 잔디가 파릇파릇 살아났어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the lawn came back fresh and green.
Lettuce has come up fresh and green in the vegetable garden.
The spring mountains have begun to turn fresh green.

examples.ko: 겨울이 지나니 나뭇가지마다 잎이 파릇파릇 나와요.
examples.en: Now that winter is over, leaves are coming out green on every branch.

explain: 갓 자라난 풀이나 잎의 싱싱한 푸른색을 말해요. '푸릇푸릇'도 비슷하게 쓰고, 한국어에서 '파랗다'는 초록색에도 쓰여서 새싹을 '파랗다'고 하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It describes the fresh green color of newly grown grass or leaves. '푸릇푸릇' is used in a similar way. In Korean '파랗다' can cover green as well, so sprouts are often described with the same root.

examples.en: Since spring came, the lawn is fresh and green.
Seeing the fresh green sprouts makes me feel good.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤 나뭇잎이 더 파릇파릇해 보여요.
examples.en: After the rain, the leaves look even fresher and greener.
I bought fresh green spinach at the market.
The lettuce in the garden grew up fresh and green.

examples.ko: 파릇파릇해진 산을 보니 봄이 온 것 같아요.
examples.en: Seeing the mountain turn fresh green, it feels like spring has come.

explain: 어리고 싱싱한 풀이나 채소의 색을 말할 때 써요. 시든 모습과 반대되는 느낌이에요. 비유로 젊고 생기 있는 사람에게도 써요.
explain_en: It is used for the color of young, fresh grass and vegetables, the opposite of a wilted look. Figuratively it can also describe a young, lively person.

examples.en: It's convenient to scoop out and eat a watermelon with a spoon.
A worm ate its way into the inside of the apple.
I scooped up the whole tub of ice cream with a spoon and ate it.

examples.ko: 아이가 감자 속만 파먹고 껍질은 남겼어요.
examples.en: The child dug out and ate only the inside of the potato and left the skin.

examples.ko: 군고구마 속을 파먹는 게 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: Scooping out and eating the inside of a roasted sweet potato is the best.
Insects ate into the roots, so the tree withered.

explain: 겉은 두고 속을 파내서 먹는 모습에 써요. 숟가락으로 먹는 음식에 잘 어울려요. 비유로 '재산을 파먹다'처럼 모아 둔 것을 조금씩 쓰는 일에도 말해요.

phrases.example: 일은 안 하고 부모님 재산만 파먹고 있어요.
phrases.en: He doesn't work and just lives off his parents' wealth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모아 둔 돈이나 재산을 벌지 않고 조금씩 쓰는 모습을 말해요. 보통 좋지 않게 보는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes spending saved money or assets bit by bit without earning anything. It usually sounds critical.
phrases.en_equiv: eat away at savings; live off one's inheritance

explain_en: It describes digging out the inside and eating it while leaving the outside. It suits foods you eat with a spoon. It is also used figuratively, as in '재산을 파먹다', for using up savings little by little.

examples.en: The village lookout guarded the gate all night.

examples.ko: 이야기 속 파수꾼은 적이 오는 걸 먼저 봤어요.
examples.en: The lookout in the story saw the enemy coming first.
The lookout shouted to warn the people.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 연극에서 성을 지키는 파수꾼 역을 했어요.
examples.en: As a child, I played the guard protecting the castle in a play.
In the forest, a squirrel keeps watch like a lookout.
He is called a guardian of democracy.

explain: 옛이야기나 연극에서 망을 보는 사람으로 자주 나와요. 요즘 일상에서는 '경비'나 '보초'라고 하고, '파수꾼'은 '민주주의의 파수꾼'처럼 무언가를 지키는 사람을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It often appears in old tales and plays as the person keeping watch. In daily life people now say '경비' or '보초', and '파수꾼' is also used figuratively for someone who protects something, as in '민주주의의 파수꾼'.

examples.en: Grandfather burst into laughter when he heard the news.

examples.ko: 사진 속 친구들이 모두 파안대소하고 있어요.
examples.en: All my friends in the photo are laughing heartily.
The audience roared with laughter watching the comedy film.

examples.ko: 우승한 선수가 파안대소하는 모습이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A scene of the winning player beaming with laughter was on the news.

examples.ko: 아이의 엉뚱한 대답에 온 가족이 파안대소해요.
examples.en: The whole family bursts into laughter at the child's silly answer.

examples.ko: 그는 농담 한마디에 파안대소하며 손뼉을 쳤어요.
examples.en: He clapped, laughing out loud at a single joke.

explain: 얼굴이 활짝 펴지도록 크게 웃는 모습이에요. 대화에서는 '크게 웃다', '활짝 웃다'라고 많이 하고, '파안대소하다'는 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요. '박장대소'는 손뼉을 치며 크게 웃는 거예요.
explain_en: It describes laughing so hard your whole face lights up. In conversation people usually say '크게 웃다' or '활짝 웃다', and '파안대소하다' appears more in writing and news. '박장대소' means laughing loudly while clapping.

examples.en: Our team swept all the way up to the final.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 파죽지세의 연승을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team keeps extending its winning streak at an unstoppable pace.
That candidate's approval rating shot up at a crushing pace.
The players pressed their opponent with overwhelming force.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 게임이 파죽지세로 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: The new game is gaining popularity at a breakneck pace.
The team that had been on an unstoppable run lost for the first time.

explain: 막을 수 없을 만큼 거침없이 이기거나 나아가는 기세예요. 대부분 '파죽지세로' 꼴로 스포츠, 선거, 인기 같은 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 한자성어라서 격식 있는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means momentum so strong nothing can stop it. It mostly appears as '파죽지세로' in news about sports, elections and popularity. As a four-character idiom, it sounds somewhat formal.

examples.en: Right before the wedding, I decided to call it off.
A small misunderstanding even led to breaking off the engagement.
Everyone was surprised to hear the news of the broken engagement.
Because of my parents' objection, we ended up calling off the engagement.

examples.ko: 파혼 후에도 두 사람은 친구로 지내요.
examples.en: Even after the broken engagement, the two of them stay friends.
There's a rumor going around that the couple called off their engagement.

explain: 결혼하기로 약속한 뒤에 그 약속을 깨는 일이에요. 결혼한 뒤에 헤어지는 '이혼'과 달라요. 동사로는 '파혼하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means breaking a promise to marry after it has been made. It differs from '이혼', which is splitting up after marriage. The verb form is '파혼하다'.

examples.ko: 이번 경기가 우승 팀을 판가름하게 돼요.
examples.en: This match will decide the winning team.
The final vote will determine the result.
What decides the outcome is stamina in the end.
It's not easy to judge who is right.
The referee's call decided the match.
This interview determines whether you pass.

explain: '결정하다'보다 두 갈래 중 어느 쪽인지 갈리는 순간에 잘 어울려요. 승부, 합격, 옳고 그름에 많이 써요. '판가름이 나다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Compared with '결정하다', it fits moments when things split into two outcomes. It is often used for the result of a match, pass or fail, and right or wrong. People also commonly say '판가름이 나다'.

examples.ko: 월급이 밀린 판국에 보너스는 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: With our pay overdue, we can't even dream of a bonus.
You're bringing up a trip in a situation like this?

examples.ko: 나라 경제가 어려운 판국이라 모두 조심해요.
examples.en: The national economy is in a tough spot, so everyone is careful.

examples.ko: 시험이 내일인 판국에 게임이 하고 싶어요?
examples.en: The exam is tomorrow and you want to play games?

examples.ko: 일이 이런 판국이 될 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't know things would end up in a state like this.

examples.ko: 판국을 보니 오늘은 일찍 퇴근하기 힘들겠어요.
examples.en: Looking at how things stand, leaving early today will be hard.

explain: '상황'과 비슷하지만 좋지 않은 일이 벌어진 형편에 주로 써요. '~ㄴ 판국에'로 많이 쓰고, 한숨이나 나무라는 느낌이 들어가요. 좋은 상황에는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '상황' but is mostly used for a bad or troubling state of affairs. It often appears as '~ㄴ 판국에' and carries a sigh or a scolding tone. It is rarely used for good situations.
